So, what you really want to do is when you move towards Asha is to constantly reinvent yourself to discover new ideas about yourself. And this is a never-ending process. Follow your heart and action will come naturally to you. When that happens, God will also come naturally to you, and you'll discover new truths, new powers, and new understandings that will bring you greater happiness in life. It's becoming—a constant process of becoming. You can't seek Asha in one lifetime; that's why we are reincarnated because we come back and move closer towards Asha each time. But there can never be an end point. Because if you reach that end point, everyone else hasn't, so you have a duty to help others move closer to Asha too. It's a constant struggle, but that gives meaning and purpose to the universe.

The fact that we're all striving to be better—virtue, truth, asha—are what we strive for. There can be no perfection; there can only be a process of becoming. The universe is a constant process of becoming, struggle, pain, and tragedy, but from that we can build hope, virtue, and goodness.

The three major civilizations—the Greeks, the Israelites, and the Persians—that came after the collapse of the Bronze Age interact with each other in complex ways. Next week, I'll show you how these civilizations interact historically.
